complexity.notes: The only change from the previous submission is pop() -> pop(0), which turns the traversal from DFS into BFS but leaves the overall cost unchanged. Each vertex visit rescans the entire edge list, and each edges.remove / vertices.remove is a linear scan, so this is far from optimal; a solution that ||builds an adjacency list once, then runs BFS/DFS with a visited set|| reaches O(V + E). On the style side, pop(0) on a list is O(len(queue)) — collections.deque with popleft() is the idiomatic fix — and iterating edges[::-1] while mutating edges works only because the slice makes a copy; iterating a copy explicitly (e.g. list(edges)) would make that intent clearer.
complexity.summary: Repeatedly pops an unvisited vertex and BFS/DFS-expands its component by scanning the full edge list, deleting each matching edge and enqueuing its endpoints, counting one component per outer iteration.
